correctness.rationale: Publisher Eqs. (6.17) and (6.20) print the same extra α in the density and in the tail integrand, but (6.20) equates its tail to E_α(−λx^α). For x>0, differentiating the entire Mittag–Leffler series after composition and cancelling αk using Γ(αk+1)=αkΓ(αk) gives f_pub=−α(d/dx)E_α(−λx^α). The boundary values at zero and infinity are 1 and 0 for 0<α≤1, so the total mass is α and the printed density's tail integral is αE_α(−λx^α). Removing α is the unique multiplicative normalization, and rescaling y=λ^(1/α)x identifies the nonnegative classical density. Equation (6.19) really does use the upper endpoint α; it is not the raw moment stated there. With the positive power-law tail in (6.22), the tail-integral formula for r>0 converges at zero and converges at infinity exactly for r<α when 0<α<1; equality diverges logarithmically. No positive integer moment is finite there. Finite lower-order fractional moments are possible and should not be confused with integer moments. At α=1 the density is correctly exponential and has all positive moments, although the finite endpoint in (6.19) would still be inappropriate. Removing the erroneous factor in (6.25) subtracts n log α, not a parameter-independent constant. VERIFICATION.md and verify_fed.py were inspected, not executed; the latter uses a finite-precision test of truncated series at a point, not an exact coefficient-wise proof, and its tail tolerance is tested on the last loop value. The analytic derivation does not depend on those checks.

value.rationale: Although normalization is elementary here, it changes the status of a proposed law, exposes the classical identity of the repair, distinguishes finite fractional moments from infinite integer moments, and changes the likelihood objective in an estimated parameter.
